$comment: The source of sf-menu-context's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/context-menu (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

position.summary: Deprecated: a menu has no tail since 1.3.0 (owner, 2026-10-12); the value is kept for its class and draws nothing.

tooltip.summary: Deprecated: a menu has no tail since 1.3.0 (owner, 2026-10-12); the value is kept for its class and draws nothing.

items.x-note: the older list form; entries is the current one

shortcut.summary: A key combination at the row's end, as sf-button's shortcut writes it (mod+c, shift+mod+z, escape, F2), drawn in the platform's words as plain glyphs; other text is shown as written.

status.summary: "danger" draws the row as a destructive action, as danger: true does: the status word of every control (decision C13); "error" is read as danger.

entries.summary: The menu as data (set as a property, or JSON in the attribute). See item_contract. When present, it replaces items and the content slot.

popup.summary: Not drawn until opened through openFor(). A menu without it is drawn in place, as before.

search.summary: {placeholder, empty, remote}: a search field above the rows (set as a property). Local by default; with remote: true the menu raises sf-context-menu-search {query} and shows the entries the host sets. A submenu entry passes it with `search`.

submenu.summary: How a row's submenu opens: flyout (a second panel beside the row, the default) or drill (the same panel shows the submenu instead of its own rows, with the way back and the parent's label in a head). A drilling panel's width never grows with the depth.

size.summary: The menu's size: rows as tall as a field of that size (32px at 1/2, 40px at 1), its text, insets, search and footer. A submenu takes its parent's size.

width.summary: How wide openFor() opens the menu, by what it holds (decision C32; the steps are core's --sf-popup-*-width, compact density moves them with the text): content (a menu: its longest line, between --sf-popup-menu-min-width and --sf-popup-menu-max-width, 10-18rem, 9-16rem compact), list (choices at a field: at least the trigger, up to --sf-popup-list-max-width or the trigger, whichever is wider), panel (a panel with a search and actions: --sf-popup-panel-width or the trigger, whichever is wider, fixed), form and form-wide (a form: --sf-popup-form-width or --sf-popup-form-wide-width; on a phone (below 44rem) a sheet at the bottom of the screen, its whole width, over the scrim; focus goes to its first field and Escape closes it), trigger (exactly the control that opened it; a long line ends in an ellipsis) or a CSS length. Every kind stays inside the screen. While open the menu publishes the trigger's width as --sf-context-menu-trigger-inline-size. openFor(anchor, {width}) overrides it.

tabs.x-note: "A|B" in the attribute; the property also takes a list [{id, label}] (the component's own accessor), one member with one type (§4.2)
tabs.summary: A panel with tabs: labels separated by |, or [{id, label}] as a property. The head (tabs and the close button) and the footer never scroll, the body does, and the panel keeps a fixed width (a ladder step, or width) whatever a tab holds.

active-tab.summary: The chosen tab's id or index; the host renders that tab's rows into the content slot.

closable.summary: A close button at the end of the panel's head.

checked.summary: The state a check or radio row asks for; null for a plain item.

group.summary: The choice row's id when an option of it was chosen.

select.summary: An entry was chosen, at any depth. Cancel it to keep the menu open.

id.summary: The setting's own name: a value row's id.

value.summary: The value the setting now has: a boolean for a switch row, a number for a range row, the chosen option's id for a choice row.

change.summary: A person asks to change a value row's setting: the request, sent before the value is written. Raised after select and only when select was not cancelled; a command row raises select alone. Cancelled, nothing changes and the row keeps the value it had -- the view never shows a value its host did not take.

id.summary: The setting's own name: a value row's id.

value.summary: The value the setting now has: a boolean for a switch row, a number for a range row, the chosen option's id for a choice row.

changed.summary: The fact of change: the value is written into its entry and the row shows it. A host that only persists what a person did listens to this one and nothing else. reset raises it once for each row it moved; set-value and set-all raise nothing, as a value set from outside is not reported back (standard §8).

reset.summary: The person asked for the declared values back: the request. Cancelled, the current values stay; otherwise the menu shows the declared ones, says changed once for each row that moved, and waits for the host to persist them, as sf-tabs-settings-reset does.

open.summary: Opened through openFor(). Bubbles and is composed; carries no detail.

close.summary: A menu opened through openFor() was closed. Bubbles and is composed; carries no detail.

search.summary: The query of a search the host answers (search.remote).

tab.summary: A tab of the panel was chosen; the host shows its rows.

offset.summary: The gap between the anchor and the menu: a token (var(--sf-space-1\/3)), a CSS length, or a number of pixels. Left out, --sf-space-1/4.

open-for.summary: Open beside an element: top layer, anchored by SF.Position with flip and shift, focus on the first item (or 'last', or 'none'). The menu then owns its lifecycle: Escape, Tab, a press outside and a choice close it and return the focus -- to where it was, or to the anchor's own control when it was nowhere.

x-returns.description: Resolves once the menu is rendered and open, to an outcome: {outcome: applied, value: true}; refused with prevented (a listener kept it closed) or invalid (the anchor is not an element); unavailable with no-surface.

toggle-for.summary: Close when already open for this anchor, otherwise openFor().

x-returns.description: Resolves to an outcome whose value says whether the menu is open afterwards: {outcome: applied, value: false} when it closed, openFor()'s outcome when it opened; refused with prevented when a listener kept it open.

close.summary: Close this menu and any submenu.

choose-tab.summary: Choose a tab by index and emit sf-context-menu-tab.

request-close.summary: Close an owned menu; for a menu its host placed, emit sf-context-menu-close for the host to close it.

set-value.summary: Write a setting's value into its own entry: the host's answer to change, or a value restored on load. The value lives in the entry and nowhere else, so there is no second map to disagree with it; the menu raises nothing. Refused when no entry carries that id.

x-returns.description: {outcome}: applied, or refused with not-found when no entry carries that id.

set-all.summary: Write a whole map of settings at once -- {id: value} -- into the entries that carry those ids: a panel restored from storage in one call rather than one set-value per row. The menu raises nothing. Refused when no id in the map is an entry's.

x-returns.description: {outcome, count}: how many entries were written; refused with not-found when none was.

show.summary: Go straight to one setting: in a drilling menu the panel opens the levels down to it (its own submenu when it has one, otherwise the level its row stands on) and the focus goes to the row. Refused when no entry carries that id; unavailable in a flyout menu, which has no level to go to.

x-returns.description: {outcome}: applied; refused with not-found; unavailable with no-levels in a flyout menu.

reset.summary: Put the declared values back -- the values the entries carried when the host set them -- and raise reset. A listener that cancels reset keeps the current values.

x-returns.description: {outcome}: applied, or cancelled when a listener cancelled reset.

x-summary: The Framework's action menu and its settings panel: data entries with icon, caption, value, shortcut, check, submenu, separator and heading, and the value rows a setting needs (switch, range, choice, a group of rows or tiles) with one change event and the set-value, set-all, reset and show actions, opened by openFor() into the top layer, anchored, with keyboard, typeahead and focus return. A host may still render its own items and own the lifecycle.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label, settings.role: host attributes, read from the host, never settings (§3.1); the menu's own role getter left the prototype's role alone

events sf-context-menu-open, sf-context-menu-close: were facts sent after the state changed (close was also the placed menu's request to its host); by §19.3 and vocabulary §4 they are the cancelable requests, and the facts are sf-context-menu-opened and sf-context-menu-closed
x-decisions: own-verb-words: search (the host is told the query) and tab (a tab chosen) are verbs of the menu alone; their words are lang events.<verb>.label.
version: 1.3.1 → 1.4.0: added the facts opened and closed, the close reason and the entries' shape; nothing removed.
type-union: tabs is one string member ("A|B" in the attribute); the component's own property also takes a list [{id, label}], so the manifest declares the attribute form (§4.2).

item-shape: entries name their fields with `of` (the fields the template and the menu read: id, text, caption, icon, avatar, initials, shortcut, kind, type, value, lang, keywords, checked, disabled, danger, current, href, keep-open, submenu, search, options); items is the older list of {text, value}.
existing-aliases: compatibility.deprecations (position, tooltip: a menu has no tail since 1.3.0) fold into aliases.json as retired rows; both settings still answer until the date.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus entries with a check, a submenu, a search and a tabbed panel; probe.json drives the arrows, Home, End, Enter, Escape and Tab (gate 16).
css-variables: the eight public variables the sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).
side-effects: portal -- an owned menu shows in the browser's top layer, and a submenu is drawn at the end of body (or of the open dialog).

layer: kind surface; it registers through core open-surface-mark while owned, so Escape and an outside press reach it only while it is the top layer; it does not trap focus (Tab leaves and closes it).

dismissing: an owned menu asks before it closes, sf-context-menu-close {reason, unsaved} (§19.3): escape, outside, close (its head's close button), api (a choice, Tab, a script). A placed menu's head button sends the same request for its host to close it, as before. The actions keep their boolean answers (openFor, toggleFor, close) until their callers move -- a leftover.

version 1.4.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 1.4.2: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.5.0 quiet-choice: the choice row's framed full-width band with its dividers was called coarse twice (owner, 2026-10-30). A choice row is now the label with its options at the row's end, sized to their content, the chosen one on a soft fill one step down the ladder; view: "band" brings the framed form back for a row that needs it. A look, not a contract: the entry's fields, its roles and its events are the same, and a choice row now keeps the level's leading column and is narrowed by a search, as every other row is.

version 1.4.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.5.0 drill: submenu says how a submenu opens -- flyout (a second panel beside the row) or drill (the same panel, a head with the way back and the parent's label). The default stays flyout, so no shipped menu changes; a settings panel is the recipe submenu="drill" with value rows (owner, 2026-10-30). A row's place in the tree is written into its markup as a path ("2/1"), so the menu reads the level from the markup and the panel's width never grows with the depth.

version 1.5.0 switch-row: a boolean setting is the row itself -- a menuitemcheckbox whose switch is drawn from the Framework switch's own track and thumb (an input inside a button is no markup at all), so the menu's roles, keyboard and roving tab stop are the ones it already has. change {id, value, previous, entry} follows an uncancelled select and changed follows the write, so a host that wants settings listens to one pair and never works out what the person did from group, checked and id. The proposal's action `set` is `set-value` here: `set` is the Smart base's own state patcher (core/js/smart-base.js), and an action of that name would shadow it.

version 1.5.0 range-row: a number in a range is a native slider at the row's end with the number after it, so the platform's own keys, pointer and announcement are the ones a person meets. A slider is not a menu item and is not given a menu role: it carries sf-context-menu-stop, which joins the menu's roving tab stop and its up/down walk while the side arrows, Home and End stay the slider's. The number under a dragged thumb follows the pointer -- the entry holds it, so the row shows what the person is doing -- and the events come when the thumb is let go, or at once from a key, which is one notch: select and change on every pixel of a drag would be a host told fifty times what happened once.

version 1.5.0 group-row: a block of rows is one entry (type: "group"), so a panel's quick settings are declared where its rows are instead of being a second list beside them. view: "rows" is a named block of the same rows; view: "tiles" is the grid the owner liked, each tile an icon, a name and the current value, so a tile needs no tooltip to be read. A tile is a row of the menu, not a control inside one: it keeps the row's class and the row's roles (menuitemcheckbox for a switch), and its geometry is reset on top, as a choice option's is. A group's items carry paths of their own ("3/1"), the step the submenu grammar already had, so the menu reads one tree.

version 1.5.0 settings-fold: sf-settings-menu 1.0.0 is removed and its work is this component's (owner decision, 2026-10-30: "Fold into sf-context-menu"). Everything it drew is a recipe of entries here -- boolean is the switch row, choice the choice row, range the range row, action a command row, section a heading, divider a separator, tile: true a group with view: "tiles", its drill template submenu="drill", its rows template the value rows, resettable the reset action with the reset event, values the entries themselves and set-all. Its change/changed pair is kept as it was -- change is the cancelable request, sent before the value is written, changed the fact after it -- and the menu's own select comes first, so a command row still raises select alone.

version 1.5.0 values: a setting's declared value is the value its entry carried when the host set the entries; reset puts those back. The snapshot is taken once, when the entries arrive, and never again from a value the person changed -- a declared value re-read after a change is not a declared value. A change is written by the row's own path, which also fixes a choice row inside a submenu or a group: the old write looked the row up by identity in the top-level list and found nothing there.

version 1.5.0 choice-drill: a choice of more or longer options than fit at a row's end is view: "drill" -- the chosen option under the label, a chevron, and the options as a level of the panel with a check mark on the chosen one; choosing one goes back to the rows, where the row now reads the new value. It is the same entry, the same id and the same change/changed pair as the quiet row, so a panel may move a row between the two looks without touching its host. The level holds no entries of its own, so nothing opens below it, and a flyout menu, which has no level to open, draws the quiet row.

version 1.5.0 panel-width: a drilling panel's width is fixed and public -- --sf-context-menu-inline-size, 280px by default (the ladder's f7 + a8), the width the owner reviewed in the prototype. A fixed width is the point of drilling: the panel neither grows with a level's longest word nor with a value, so a long label wraps and a long value is cut with the whole of it in title. openFor(anchor, {width}) still overrides it, as it does for a panel with tabs.

version 1.5.4: a header's initials without a picture are sf-avatar's rule (helpers/text.js getInitials, smart helpers 1.0.4; reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 10): a preposition after the first word is skipped, a hyphenated single name reads as its parts and a letter outside the basic plane is whole. The row and header avatar markup is unchanged.

version 1.6.0: the tag is sf-menu-context (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.menu-context and the bundle cl-menu-context follow it. sf-context-menu stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-menu-context, sf-context-menu) (change journal tag-sf-context-menu-to-sf-menu-context, path-smart-context-menu-to-menu-context).

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-07): a minor (a look; settings, values, events and keys unchanged). A menu with a search keeps its field where it is and scrolls its rows alone (docs review R012, R013; component.context-menu 1.2.0). The rows of a menu with search -- the top level, a flyout submenu, a drilling level, the empty note -- stand in .sf-context-menu-list, a scroll area of their own under the field, and the content carries sf-context-menu-content--search (not the root, whose class list openFor() writes sf-context-menu--open into); the content no longer scrolls, so the field (and a drilling level's head) stays on top and the scrollbar starts under it. The field has 8px (space-1/3, a step after the panel's 4px) on every side, at both sizes. A menu without search draws as before. How a chosen row is marked (owner decision R016): the chosen row of a pick-one list -- kind: "radio" rows, a drilled choice's options -- carries sf-context-menu-item--chosen, the soft fill of the chosen (secondary container: fill 12 light, 24 dark; its hover the next step, 16/28), and no check mark; a ticked row (kind: "check") leads with its check in the icons' column at their width, the level keeping that column when any row can be ticked, and shows its own icon while unticked. No row keeps an empty column at its end for a mark any more, so rows reach the end padding. The quiet choice row's options, switch rows and tiles are unchanged.

version 1.7.1 (2026-11-07): a patch (docs thread, bus msg-da670440b2ce4ad2a802). A search the host answers (search.remote) keeps the menu open whatever the host answers: a host that set no entries for a query took the field, and the focus in it, out of the page and the surface drew nothing, so the menu looked closed and the keys went to the body. A menu with a search now draws its field and the rows' area when its entries are empty, and a host-searched menu with no rows shows search.empty under the field whatever the field holds (an answer to an older query can arrive after the field was cleared). Rows set again after an empty answer are drawn under the same field, which keeps the focus and what was typed. The class lists stay as they were while the entries are empty: the root's sf-context-menu--entries class followed a non-empty list, so the class list openFor() wrote sf-context-menu--open into was written again without it and the surface hid. A wheel turned past the end of the rows no longer scrolls the page behind the menu: the content, the rows' area under a search and a panel's body carry overscroll-behavior: contain (component.context-menu 1.2.1; admin.simai.io profile language). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged; probe context-menu-host-search.

version 1.7.2 (2026-11-07): a patch (owner R017, R018; component.context-menu 1.3.0, core.runtime 1.31.1). The panel's inset is its search field's: 8px (space-1/3, the defaults of --sf-context-menu-padding-inline and -block), so the field, the rows and their hover and chosen fills, a drilling head and the footer share one edge; a row's text keeps its axis (the rows' inset gives back the panel's). The rows' scroll area under a search still spans the panel, so its scrollbar stands at the panel's edge. A menu whose rows all fit no longer shows a scrollbar: position() clamped a panel to the room by its trigger half a pixel or a few pixels short of its height, so it overflowed by a sliver and a scrollbar with a full-track thumb stood beside rows that fit; a panel that misses its room by no more than the edge's padding now takes its whole height, rounded up. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged; probe context-menu-inset-overflow.

version 1.8.0 (2026-11-07): a minor. openFor() and toggleFor() take an offset option, the gap between the anchor and the menu as a token, a length or pixels (simai/ui-source#69; before, a fixed --sf-space-1/4). An anchor that draws no box of its own -- a Smart host, display: contents, such as sf-button-icon or sf-button -- is measured by the boxes it draws (core SF.Position, core.runtime 1.32.0), so the menu opens under the button instead of at the window's left edge, and width trigger takes the button's width (simai/ui-source#68).

version 1.9.0 (2026-11-07): a minor (a look and one public variable; settings, values, events and keys unchanged; owner C05-C07, docs review R029, which replaces R017's 1/3 inset; component.context-menu 1.4.0, core.runtime 1.36.0). A row's highlight stands --sf-space-1/4 from the panel's edge (the defaults of --sf-context-menu-padding-inline and -block, 1/3 before), is as tall as a control of the menu's step (--sf-ui-1/2--control-height, --sf-ui-1--control-height) and rounded --sf-radius--ui (the new public --sf-context-menu-row-radius); its icon and text stand --sf-space-1/2 inside it, the icon --sf-space-1/2 before the text. Headings, notes, value rows, a drilling head, a header, the footer, a panel's rows and sf-button items start on the same line. A search is the panel's header, not a boxed field: a search icon (new markup: i.sf-context-menu-search-icon before the input), no frame and no fill, a row's height and the inset above and below, its icon and text exactly over the rows' icon and text, a hairline across the panel's width under it that turns primary while the field has the focus; it stays put and only the rows scroll. The scrollbar shows only when the rows do not fit (1.7.2); while it takes room in the layout the scrolling area (the content, or the rows' area under a search) gives up its inline-end padding -- class sf-context-menu-content--scrollbar or sf-context-menu-list--scrollbar, set from offsetWidth - clientWidth through a ResizeObserver -- and the track is the inset, a thumb of --sf-space-1/4 and the inset again (::-webkit-scrollbar; Firefox thin), so the thumb is as far from the highlight as the highlight is from the panel's other edge. An overlay scrollbar keeps the inset. Probes context-menu-inset-overflow, context-menu-search-scroll.

version 1.9.1 (2026-11-07): a patch, no change to what is drawn (component.context-menu 1.4.1). The scrollbar's mark (sf-context-menu-content--scrollbar, sf-context-menu-list--scrollbar) is written by the shared component/panel-scrollbar.js, which sf-dropdown, sf-input-lookup and sf-profile-picker use too; the track, the search header and the inset come from the shared partial component/context-menu/scss/_panel.scss (owner C05-C07, R029).

version 1.9.2 (2026-11-08): a patch (simai/ui-source#72). Enter in the search field chooses the first row the query left, as a combobox does: the row is pressed, so a command row selects and the menu closes, a submenu row opens its submenu and a drilling row goes a level in -- in an opened menu and in a drilling panel the page placed. A query that left no row, and an Enter that ends a word an input method is composing, do nothing. The key is taken (preventDefault) and still bubbles, so a host that answered Enter in the field itself (sf-content-editor 1.1.1) can see the menu did and drop its own handler. Before, the field kept every key but Escape, Tab and ArrowDown, and the person had to press ArrowDown before Enter. Settings, values and events unchanged; probe context-menu-search-enter.

version 1.10.0 (2026-11-08): a minor (owner decision 2026-11-07, docs review R030, rule C04; component.kbd 1.1.0, component.context-menu 1.4.2). An entry's shortcut is written as sf-button's is -- mod+c, shift+mod+z, escape, F2 -- and drawn in this platform's words: on an Apple platform the glyphs side by side (⇧⌘Z), elsewhere words joined with + (Ctrl+Shift+Z); a value that is not that notation (⇧⌘L, «Ctrl K») is shown as written. The keys are the kbd component's: <kbd class="sf-kbd--group sf-context-menu-item-shortcut"> with a <kbd> per key; inside a menu the kbd sheet draws them as plain glyphs, 0.875em, in --sf-on-surface-variant (a disabled entry's in its ink). The menu sheet no longer styles them; kbd is a relation.
version 1.11.0: an entry takes status: "danger" ("error" read as its alias), the status word every control uses (owner decision C13, docs review R031); danger: true keeps working.

version 1.12.0 (2026-11-08; one number above the unreleased 1.11.0 and 1.10.1 it joins): a patch (C06, DEV measurement of the docs on ui-0c23f6a0af12; component.context-menu 1.4.3). In a menu without a leading column (no row has an icon, a tick or a picture) the search header's text stands over the rows' text and its icon at the header's end; the text stood a search icon and a gap (24-28px) right of the rows'. With a leading column nothing changes. Settings, entries, events and keys are unchanged.

version 1.13.4: the menu stands over the page: the overlay place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08) through the class context menu (component.context-menu 1.5.0) -- --sf-shadow-overlay on --sf-surface-popup, two layers at black 16 and 8 in the light theme where level 3 drew three at 24, 12 and 8. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives each action's method its one object argument, close({reason}), setValue({id, value}), setAll({values}), show({id}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object); the element's code also takes the value alone, show(<string>), and the reference says so (x-registry.action-calls). openFor(anchor, options?), toggleFor(anchor, options?) and chooseTab(index) stay positional in the reference, as the element's methods take them: openFor and toggleFor want the anchor element first, chooseTab the index (x-registry.action-calls positional). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a submenu placed on the body takes the density of the menu it opens from (density, decision C22): a compact menu opens compact submenus. Also: a patch, nothing drawn differently. openFor, toggleFor and chooseTab take the object form of their action too (standard §4.4): openFor({anchor, options}) opens, where it threw a TypeError, and chooseTab({index}) chooses, where it did nothing. The runtime gives the class-written methods that form (elementFromManifest's positional, core.runtime 1.43.0); the positional calls stay as they were. openFor and toggleFor answer an outcome (§4.4), not a boolean: applied with value true or false (open afterwards), refused with prevented or invalid, unavailable with no-surface; an anchor that is not an element is refused instead of thrown. A caller that tested the boolean reads `answer === true || answer?.outcome === 'applied'` (core effects, the sortable inserter and sf-settings do). The reference gives the three one object argument (x-registry.action-calls no longer says positional). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a patch (decision C22). A menu opened by openFor() or toggleFor() takes the density of the control that opens it: its panel is drawn where the menu element stands -- often on the body, outside the compact region of the toolbar or table that opens it -- so two menus of one compact page drew at two sizes (DEV, 2026-11-09). The panel carries data-sf-density of the opener's region (normal outside any) while open; a size the page gave the menu still wins; a submenu follows the panel it opens from. Settings, values, events and the drawing are unchanged; probe tooltip-light (two menus).

Since the menu came from its component.json (2026-10-27) the property has been kept by the manifest's accessor (core element-manifest.js), and the template read the list from the props, which gave the default, an empty list: the panel opened as an empty box of 10 by 10 px with nothing to focus, so Escape (the menu's own, from inside it) had nothing to start from. fields.caption: string, a second line under the label
fields.value: string, read-only value at the row's end; on a drilling row it is drawn under the label, where a long value is cut instead of widening the panel
fields.shortcut: string, a key combination shown at the row's end as plain glyphs: written as sf-button's (mod+c, shift+mod+z, F2) and drawn in the platform's words; other text as written
fields.status: 'danger' (or its alias 'error'), the same as danger: true -- the controls' status word (C13)
fields.current: boolean, the place the person is
fields.submenu: entries: opened beside the row, or in place of the panel's own rows when the menu says submenu="drill"
fields.keepOpen: boolean, a choice does not close the menu
fields.lang: string, the language the label is written in
fields.search: {placeholder, empty}, a field above the submenu that narrows its rows by label, caption and keywords
fields.keywords: string, extra words a search matches
fields.avatar: string, a picture URL drawn in the lead (a site's logo, a person)
fields.initials: string, drawn in the lead when there is no picture

fields.text: string, names the items under it

fields.caption: string or string[], the lines under it
fields.initials: string, drawn without a picture (from the name by default)

fields.text: string, the group's name, drawn at the start of the row
fields.icon: string, a Material Symbols name in the lead
fields.caption: string, a second line under the name
fields.view: 'quiet' (the default: the options at the row's end, sized to their content, no frame and no dividers, the chosen one on a soft fill), 'band' (the framed full-width band, for a row that must show every option across the panel) or 'drill' (the chosen option under the label and a chevron; the options open as a level of the panel, a check mark on the chosen one, and choosing goes back -- for a list too long or too wordy to stand at the row's end). A drilling view needs a drilling panel: in a flyout menu the row stays the quiet one
fields.options: [{id, text, icon, checked, disabled}], side by side; a choice is marked at once and the menu stays open unless keepOpen is false

fields.id: string, the setting's own name, reported as id in change
fields.caption: string, a second line under the label
fields.icon: string, a Material Symbols name in the lead
fields.value: boolean, the setting's own value and its only home; the row is a menuitemcheckbox and the switch at its end is drawn, not a second control
fields.keepOpen: boolean, false closes the menu on a change; a setting is tried rather than committed, so the menu stays open by default

fields.id: string, the setting's own name, reported as id in change
fields.caption: string, a second line under the label
fields.icon: string, a Material Symbols name in the lead
fields.value: number, the setting's own value and its only home
fields.min: number, the lowest value (0 by default)
fields.max: number, the highest value (100 by default)
fields.step: number, how far one key or one notch moves it (1 by default)
fields.unit: string, written after the number (%, px)

fields.text: string, names the block for a screen reader
fields.view: 'rows' (the default: a block of rows) or 'tiles' (a grid of tiles, each an icon, a name and the current value)
fields.items: entries: the rows of the block, of any row kind -- a switch, a range, a choice, a command row or a row with a submenu

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-context-menu for every action menu: give it entries and open it with openFor(anchor). It opens below and start-aligned by default, with no tail, in the top layer, on the profile menu's surface. A profile menu is one: a header for the person, a choice row for the theme, a submenu with search for the language. A settings panel is one too, and is this component rather than a tag of its own: submenu="drill" with value rows (switch, range, choice, a group of tiles), listening to sf-context-menu-change alone.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not hand-make a menu of divs and buttons: the row geometry, roles, keyboard and focus return are this component's
Do not ask for a tail: position and tooltip are deprecated and draw nothing
Do not keep a second map of the settings' values: a value lives in its entry, and set-value writes it there
Do not store a setting yourself: the menu shows it and raises change; the host persists it

accessibility.focus: Rows rendered from entries carry menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio with aria-checked, and aria-haspopup/aria-expanded for a submenu; one roving tab stop. Opened through openFor(): the anchor gets aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; Escape closes one level and returns the focus to its row or the anchor; in a drilling menu Escape and the outward arrow first go one level back, to the row the level was opened from, and close the menu only at the top level; Tab closes the whole chain; a letter moves to the next item it starts. A host that renders the menu itself owns opening, Escape/Tab dismissal and focus return, as before. A header and a note are text. The options of a choice row are menuitemradio in a group, walked by the side arrows. A searchable menu opens on its field, which keeps the letters and the side arrows; ArrowDown goes on to the rows. A switch row is the menuitemcheckbox itself, with aria-checked for its value and Enter or Space to turn it; a range row's slider is the platform's, named by the label, announced with its unit and moved by the side arrows, Home and End, while ArrowUp and ArrowDown stay the menu's walk; a group is a group with its own name, and a tile of it is a row of the menu with the row's role.

deprecations.replacement: openFor(anchor, {side, align}) places the menu; no tail is drawn
none: a menu has no tail

focus.summary: Focus the current available item. A host that renders the menu itself waits for rendering and owns opening and dismissal.
